title: The duplicate order
summary: Model idempotent processing so a retried request does not charge a customer twice.

scenario.briefing: A network timeout caused the client to retry an order request. The API charged the customer twice. Design a deduplication state and review a proposed patch before it is deployed.

objectives.description: Model accepted order ids and the accepted count.
Find the ordering flaw in the proposed patch.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Process A1 once, try A1 again, then process B2.
A duplicate must not increase the accepted count.
The patch records the id after charging, so a crash between those steps can still double-charge.
Set processed to A1, then B2; accepted becomes 2. In review, reject the patch because the side effect happens before the id is recorded.

misconceptions.description: Recording the id after the side effect.
misconceptions.feedback: If the process dies after charging but before recording the id, the retry charges again. Record or reserve the id before the irreversible side effect.

misconceptions.description: Treating a retry as a harmless second order.
misconceptions.feedback: A retry represents the same intent. Processing it twice charges twice. Idempotency makes the repeated request safe.

sections.title: Retries are normal
sections.body: Networks time out. Clients retry. A retried request may reach the server even when the first response was lost, so the server must decide whether it has already processed that intent. A stable idempotency key identifies the same request across attempts.

sections.title: Order side effects carefully
sections.body: A charge is an irreversible side effect. If the system records the request after charging, a crash in between leaves no memory of the charge. The record must be created atomically with the side effect, or reserved before it, so a retry can be recognized.

vocabulary.definition: Safe to repeat with the same result.
A stable identifier for one intended operation.
A change outside the function's return value, such as a charge.

steps.title: Simulate the retry cache
steps.prompt: Apply operations so A1 is processed once, its retry is ignored, and B2 is processed. The accepted count must reach 2.
steps.explanation: The retry leaves processed and accepted unchanged. A new id is added once.

steps.title: Review the retry patch
steps.prompt: Inspect the proposed order handler. Select every supported finding, then choose a verdict.

artifact.title: Proposed retry handler
artifact.caption: The patch is intended to prevent duplicate charges.

findings.label: Two simultaneous requests can both pass the lookup before either saves.
A crash after charging but before saving loses the record, so a retry charges again.
The charge and the record are not created atomically.
The initial lookup is useless and should be removed.
The patch is safe because it checks for an existing order.

verdicts.label: Reject until the id is reserved atomically before charging and retries return the recorded result
Add a console log and ship

steps.explanation: A lookup followed by a separate charge and save has race and crash windows. The idempotency record must be created atomically with, or before, the side effect.

steps.title: Retry safety

statements.label: A retry with the same idempotency key represents the same intended operation.
Recording the operation and performing its side effect must be coordinated.
Processing a retry twice is always harmless.
A stored result can be returned for a duplicate request.

steps.explanation: Idempotency records intent and result so retries are recognized. The record and side effect must be ordered safely.

accessibility.summary: The retry cache is shown as labeled state cells. Findings and verdict use standard checkboxes and radio controls.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Apply operations with Enter or Space. Review findings with Tab and Space.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each operation announces its effect. Findings list whether they are supported after submission, and the verdict feedback is read.
